purpose: Attribute observed SQLite Connection.execute and Cursor.fetchall/fetchone builtin call counts and instrumented elapsed spans to fixed LM source sites, so the aggregate execute/fetch profile can be separated into FTS, metadata, novelty and source-related boundaries. This is one mechanism diagnostic on existing old data, not a candidate comparison, speed estimate, formal performance run or fresh evaluation.

runtime.policy: Keep all LM runtime bytes and ordinary sqlite3 classes/connection/cursor/row factories unchanged. The source-binding reference supplies immutable identity and prior correctness evidence only; the completed LM execution binding/claim/DBs are never reused.

prior_evidence.disposition: The complete LM result preserves4732 profile payloads and4096 paired calls/2048 pairs, with GM p95 improvement4.791840281283378% and public native char4000 p95 improvement5.430823483528835%, below original10% goals. Keep every cell, including public-token512 p95 regression3.7551% and smaller p50 increases; absence of >5% adverse cells is not universal improvement. The new diagnostic cannot replay or replace that result.

inherited_protocol.allowed_reuse: Import the unchanged original CONFIGS and fingerprint; use the unchanged benchmark_default_recall.dataset and its pinned closure. Preserve the original cohort/config/query order, exact recall kwargs and one freshly constructed MemoryBook per cohort with four configurations in the same process. Reuse the proven source-export separation, strict inventory guards, exact Git reads/gzip checks and serialized non-force publication logic.
inherited_protocol.producer_boundary: The old helper calls cProfile.enable/disable for every recall, which would replace sys.setprofile. Do not run both or monkeypatch cProfile. A new independently named producer uses the same loop/settings with the new observer instead; original helper bytes stay untouched. Its own script SHA is recorded honestly. Never label new output as produced by the original helper or forge its script_sha256.
inherited_protocol.comparison_validator: A small new diagnostic-specific validator must preserve every existing profile_audit row/count/order/data/hash predicate while checking the new producer identity and reporting callsite tables instead of cProfile top-N statistics. It may not change the original validator/helper or fabricate the original producer's hash.

sequence.query_order: For each cohort copy dataset.queries and call random.Random(41061).shuffle exactly once; reuse that complete order for all four configurations, as the unchanged original helper does.
sequence.lifecycle: One persistent measurement worker for the complete two-cohort/eight-cell sequence. Build each cohort's fresh LM database once and retain the same MemoryBook across its four configurations. Tokenizer warmup, database creation and ingestion occur with the observer disabled. Do not split configurations into new processes or rebuild their database.
sequence.dataset_identity: Require the original frozen sessions/query counts, dataset fingerprints and query-order digests before calls. Download only the already-used pinned LoCoMo source; never select or decode fresh rows.

payload_reference.audit: Read only the exact manifest and eight gzip blobs through git show. Verify compressed sizes/SHA and raw SHA before calls. Keep all4732 query IDs and full response fingerprints excluding only latency_ms, using the original fingerprint function. Validate all eight cells, complete orders, dataset identities and every saved C2 digest. No reference retrieval is rerun.

observer.API: sys.setprofile in the single measured thread, using c_call/c_return/c_exception. Refuse an already active profile callback. Enable only around one original recall and always restore the prior None callback in finally.
observer.identification: Recognize ordinary bound builtins by the exact sqlite3 receiver class and method identity/name. Only read code/frame metadata and ephemeral receiver identity to pair events. Never inspect SQL text, arguments, frame locals, query text, returned rows, cursor contents or user strings.

rules.meaning: Exact/stem candidate routes share this source site and remain combined; no SQL or local table-name inspection.
Disambiguate shared fetch helper by frozen upper callsite; line253 is shipping native tuple path, line257 is fallback.
Same fetch helper, distinguished from FTS by upper callsite.
Initial execute boundary for FTS body tokens used by novelty/temporal reranking. Implicit cursor iteration is not fully timed by this observer.
Initial execute boundary for selected original pages. Subsequent implicit cursor iteration is outside this measured builtin boundary.
Bounded stem-FTS highlight for actual excerpts.
Initial execute boundary for original turn units in token-budget recall. Subsequent implicit iteration is outside this measured builtin boundary.
Registered use_cache=False/cache_size=0 forbids these paths; preserve and invalidate any unexpected activation.
Registered coverage=False forbids optional coverage FTS calls.
semantic=False/follow_titles=False; retain any unexpected event and invalidate the fixed-policy run.

observer.raw_event_preservation: Retain every observed target C-call span and exception outcome, with stable per-query call sequence/parent sequence, method, site ID, start/end monotonic ns, inclusive ns and nested-child/exclusive ns. Keep all sites and cells; no top-N truncation. Grouping tables are derived from these raw spans and reconciled with per-query/per-cell totals.
observer.nesting: Use a strict LIFO stack for every tracked SQLite C builtin. Pair returns/exceptions with the original receiver/method/frame identity; retain partial unmatched events on failure. For nested calls report inclusive and exclusive sums separately so totals never silently double-count nested time.
observer.unknowns: Keep any delivered ordinary SQLite builtin outside the three primary methods, and any source site not matched by the frozen rules, in explicit other/unclassified buckets with original frame metadata. Never infer categories from SQL values or silently drop unmatched events. Classification coverage gaps remain visible.
observer.native_guard: No proxy/subclass, monkeypatch, cursor wrapper, factory replacement, SQLite trace callback or Python line/opcode tracing. Assert the exact LM ordinary connection/native_db/text_factory/row_factory identities outside observation and recheck afterward. Report _candidate_rows line253 versus257 from callback metadata; the observer itself never assigns either factory.
observer.callback_failures: Observer callback errors, mismatched event pairs, impossible negative spans or a nonempty target stack after recall invalidate the stage; preserve available rows/events and stop without retry.

limitations.implicit_iteration: Implicit Cursor iteration in novelty (store.py1016-1019), selected original pages (1100-1104) and original turns (1150-1153) can execute further sqlite3_step work without a sys.setprofile c_call to fetchall/fetchone. Their recorded execute spans are not complete query-consumption times.
limitations.no_total_sql_claim: Report only observed builtin boundaries. Any recall wall time outside reconciled exclusive spans remains explicitly unattributed: Python work, implicit cursor iteration, SQLite work outside these observable methods and profiler overhead. Do not label this residual Python-only or claim the categories exhaust all SQL cost.
limitations.route_boundary: The exact and stem candidate routes share the same code callsite; keep them combined under FTS candidates. No query/table local is inspected to split them.
limitations.timing: All elapsed values include instrumentation effects and scheduling. They are mechanism observations, never unprofiled latency estimates, formal p50/p95 improvements, cross-host comparisons or a replacement for the completed LM benchmark.
limitations.span_content: A timed native builtin boundary can include its Python callbacks, thread scheduling and observer effects. Even exclusive target spans are not a direct measure of SQLite CPU time.

overhead.clock: time.perf_counter_ns; record time.get_clock_info('perf_counter'), Python/SQLite/runtime environment and the precise clock placement. Capture target end timestamp first on matching return/exception; freeze the start-timestamp placement in the reviewed implementation.
overhead.accounting: Record total callback counts by event kind, target/non-target counts and callback bookkeeping elapsed ns separately. Callback bookkeeping excludes unknown CPython dispatch cost and is not a complete overhead correction.
overhead.artificial_calibration: One fixed artificial preflight batch only, outside the corpus: retain1000 adjacent clock-pair deltas and128 native SELECT1/one-row-fetch observations with callback off followed by128 with callback on, in a separate invented in-memory DB. Save all observations and fixed order; do not choose a best repetition or adjust corpus spans with these values.
overhead.interpretation: The calibration exposes clock/Python/callback costs for that invented operation only. It is not an engine performance comparison and cannot recover uninstrumented LM timings.

artificial_proof_requirements: Real native sqlite3 c_call/c_return pairs and c_exception on an invented failing query; no SQL string or parameter value appears in outputs.

Nested real C events using a Python SQLite UDF and a second ordinary connection; exact nesting, inclusive/exclusive sums and exception unwind. No such UDF/connection is installed into a measured LM book.
Deterministic fake-clock observer fixtures prove arithmetic, mismatched pairs, nonempty-stack failure and exception preservation without treating an arbitrary timing sample as a speed gate.

Fixed filename/function/line/upper-callsite classification, including two callers of the shared _candidate_rows fetch helper, multiline call positions and explicit unknown sites. Use the actual exact LM export with invented input for integration proof.

Eligible artificial real MemoryBook recall still reaches _candidate_rows native tuple-fetch line253, restores the shipping cursor row factory, retains the same ordinary connection identity, and produces the full same payload with observer on/off. Unsupported/fallback guards are not bypassed.

Reference audit fixtures reject missing/extra/reordered/duplicate queries, changed dataset/source/helper/producer hashes, bad full-payload digests and wrong configuration axes while retaining mismatches.

Artificial publication and interruption fixtures show cell intent is remotely verified before execution, output is saved before the next cell, ambiguous publication stops, and a started/incomplete stage cannot be resumed or repeated.

execution_plan.runtime_environment: One ubuntu24.04/Python3.12 hosted VM, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and the unchanged mcp1.30.0/pydantic2.14.3/tiktoken0.12.0/regex2026.11.9 pins. Sparse/shallow code checkout; fetch only exact needed commits/blobs, never checkout all historical reports.
execution_plan.preclaim: Require an exact committed new diagnostic binding for source/evaluator/category-map/scope bytes, successful artificial observer CI and immutable prior LM source review/full result audit. A missing or mismatched binding must fail before result claim, download or any corpus call. Do not reuse the already completed LM claim or state.
execution_plan.source_isolation: Run artificial observer/native-guard correctness in a separate exact LM source export and preserve its complete inventory/archive. Create a new clean measurement export and verify all18 source files plus the aggregate before the worker and every cell. No measured source is imported or changed by correctness fixtures.
execution_plan.checkpoints: Publish one unique attempt claim. Publish source/preflight/reference/calibration receipts. The one persistent worker is the sole publisher while it runs: before each cell it writes and publishes its immutable intent, reads back the exact remote HEAD, then makes the original calls; after the cell it writes raw rows/spans plus all summaries and publishes their hashes before the next cell. The parent does not publish concurrently and reads the shared expected-head journal after the worker exits.
execution_plan.query_ledger: Write and fsync a per-query started record before enabling the observer; after disabling it retain complete payload digest and all observer spans as a finished record. Raw C data is flushed outside the observed recall boundary. On failure save the in-flight observer buffer and partial report; no extra recall is used to repair a record.
execution_plan.preservation: Lossless gzip with raw/compressed hashes for full per-cell rows, spans and final report; preserve available partial JSON/JSONL/log.partial and failure receipts. Keep all counts/categories and negative outcomes. The workflow always step exports/publishes only completed files or partial evidence and never calls retrieval.
execution_plan.no_replay: Only run_attempt1 on the exact unique trigger. Refuse existing result/state/worker or cell intent. A failed or ambiguous push stops all further calls, without automatic write retry. Any code correction after a started diagnostic needs a separately reviewed prospective attempt; this attempt is never replayed.
execution_plan.publication_boundary: Per-cell remote persistence; each query is locally fsynced. A hard VM loss may lose the current cell's unpushed local bytes, but its published intent marks it incomplete and forbids replay. Do not claim per-event remote durability.

report_contract.summaries: Per cell and per frozen category/callsite/method: calls, successful returns, C exceptions, inclusive/exclusive ns sums, callback counts/bookkeeping cost, classification gaps, native versus fallback fetch-site counts and diagnostic recall wall totals. Optional percentages may be only shares of observed exclusive builtin spans, clearly named; no speed comparison.
report_contract.equality: Full C2 payload/order audit is mandatory. Payload mismatches remain in output and invalidate the final diagnostic. No timing-based early stopping or deletion is allowed; fatal runtime/observer/source/publication errors stop and preserve the complete observed prefix.

approval_boundary: Submit and review this scope/design first. Do not implement the observer, run artificial diagnostic code, create the diagnostic workflow trigger or execute the4732-call diagnostic until root separately authorizes the next stage. Original runtime/helpers/scopes/results/gates remain unchanged.
